To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the production of extremely energetic protons is strongly enhanced in central heavy ion reactions at intermediate energy, and that the multiplicity of extremely energetic proton increases quadratically with the participant number.

(1) The extremely energetic proton emission has a strong dependence on centrality, (2) the emission is enhanced by a factor of 10-20 compared to one-body emission, (3) the extremely energetic protons are emitted preferentially in the direction of the reaction plane, and (4) the extremely energetic proton emission is enhanced by about 30-40% in the direction of participant nucleons.
the extremely energetic proton emission is enhanced strongly in central heavy-ion collisions at intermediate energies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the nuclear matter properties in the high density region of nuclear matter, which is created in heavy ion collisions at low and intermediate bombarding energies.
the study of particle emission in the intermediate energy heavy ion collision region, where a new phase of matter, the quark-gluon plasma, may be created.
the investigation of the production of extremely energetic protons in heavy-ion collisions at intermediate energy, and the search for the onset of a new reaction mechanism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the enhancement is due to the collective flow of the participant nucleons in the reaction.

in central heavy ion reactions, at intermediate energies, the extremely energetic proton production is strongly enhanced by the collective flow and by the formation of a dense and highly excited nuclear system.
the enhancement is a genuine collective phenomenon, but its origin is still a mystery.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proton emission is enhanced by a factor of about 100 in the central collisions, as compared to the one-proton removal cross section of the projectile-like fragments.
the extremely energetic proton production is strongly correlated to the reaction centrality, and the extremely energetic proton emission is a good probe of the collective motion in the reaction.
the production of extremely energetic protons is a very sensitive probe of the reaction dynamics in central heavy ion collision.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proton emission is dominated by the collective motion of the nucleons in the reaction zone.
a large number of protons with energies up to 200 MeV are produced in heavy-ion collisions, even at intermediate energies.
a strong enhancement of the extremely energetic proton production is observed in central heavy-ion collisions at intermediate energies.
